meta.titleDefault: Edura — the operating ledger for Egyptian teaching centers
meta.description: Attendance, subscriptions, payments and settlement for centers, teachers, students and guardians — in one append-only ledger.

hero.title: Your center, your teachers, your students — in one ledger
hero.subtitle: Edura runs attendance, subscriptions, payments and settlement — from the center's front desk to the guardian's phone.

cta.title: Put your center in one ledger.
cta.body: Create an account and set up your first hall, teacher and group. Nothing to install.

owners.title: The money settles itself — and you can see every step
owners.body: Cash at the counter and card online land in one book. Each lesson splits between you, the teacher and the platform the moment it completes.

counter.title: A student arrives. You have their code, and a queue behind them.
counter.body: Search by code, phone or name. If they aren't covered for this lesson, the cash step happens in the same flow — not a second screen with a modal in between.

settlement.title: One lesson, split three ways, exactly once
settlement.body: When a lesson completes, the engine claims it with a single conditional write. A lesson cannot be settled twice, and the arithmetic is the same one this diagram draws.
settlement.note: Rates below are the platform's published defaults, read live from commission settings.

halls.title: Your hall, your rate — up to the published ceiling
halls.body: Price a hall as a share of the whole room, or per attending student. The teacher sees that rate on the hall card before booking, so nothing is discovered at settlement.

ledger.title: The book cannot be edited or deleted
ledger.body: Transactions, points, settlements and the audit log all carry REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE at the database. A correction is a new, reversing entry — never a quiet edit.

team.title: Staff accounts with preset permissions, and a name on every action
team.body: Receptionist, manager and accountant each get their own scope. What a role cannot do is absent from their screen, not greyed out — and every write records who did it.

teachers.title: Take the register in a minute — even with no signal
teachers.body: Your groups, your schedule, your grades and your wallet in one place. Marks taken offline queue on the device and sync themselves when the connection returns.

register.title: Open the lesson, mark the room
register.body: Every session for your groups, with the ones already completed clearly behind you.

offline.title: The connection drops. The register does not.
offline.body: Marks are stored on the device with their own commit state, so you can see per record whether it reached the server. Conflicts resolve server-wins on sync.

door.title: A second check-in at the hall door
door.body: Turn it on and a student who passed the front desk but never reached the room shows as counter-only — visibly not present, and not counted in the lesson's split.

wallet.title: Your wallet moves with every completed lesson
wallet.body: Teaching independently settles the moment the student pays, minus the platform's commission. Teaching in a hall settles when the lesson completes.

assistants.title: An assistant who can do everything except touch your money
assistants.body: Attendance, grades, materials and schedules. Never your wallet, your payouts or your financial settings — and every action is recorded as theirs, on your behalf.

students.title: Your year, your track, your subjects — already filled in
students.body: Pick your academic year and track once. Your subjects come from the real Egyptian catalog, not a list somebody typed.

subjects.title: Choose a track, get your subjects
subjects.body: Systems, stages, grades and tracks come from the seeded catalog. Browse everything when you need to; your own subjects are the default.

plans.title: By the month, or by the lesson
plans.body: Each course sets which plans it offers. Pay online, from your wallet, or in cash at the center counter.

wallet.title: Your balance is a sum, not a stored number
wallet.body: Every top-up and every payment is an entry in an append-only ledger, and the balance is what those entries add up to. The database refuses to let it go negative.

schedule.title: Your week, on your phone
schedule.body: Sessions, halls and teachers, with attendance and grades recorded against each one.

points.title: Points for showing up and keeping up
points.body: Attendance, paying online, booking and rating all award points from the platform's own rules. The points ledger cannot be edited either.

parents.title: Minor by default — protection is on before anyone sets it
parents.body: A student counts as an adult only with a verified date of birth showing 18 or over. Missing or unverified means minor, and oversight is already active.

safety.title: The gate is closed until a guardian can be reached
safety.body: A minor with no guardian email cannot message teachers, assistants or center staff. A phone number is not enough — email is the only channel we can actually deliver on today.

narrow.title: Classes, materials, grades and the wallet all keep working
narrow.body: Only adult-facing conversations are closed, and the child can always reach their own guardian. The account is never suspended by this rule, and the deadline escalates a reminder — it never punishes.

oversight.title: Read-only, and the limits are the feature
oversight.body: Approved links, minor children, adult threads only — and a banner both sides can see. It never marks a message read and has no write path in the interface or the API.

pay.title: Pay for your child's lesson from your own wallet
pay.body: Who paid is recorded on the payment. Where the money goes does not change, so every split, statement and payout behaves exactly as it would have.

follow.title: Attendance, progress and fees per child
follow.body: Notifications when an absence is marked, a grade is entered or a payment is recorded.

trust.title: The interface tells the truth about what the software guarantees
trust.body: Every claim on this page points at a mechanism in the database or the code, not at a policy document.

append.title: Seven tables the application cannot rewrite
append.body: Transactions, points, the audit log and settlements are INSERT and SELECT only. Invoices, payouts and the blacklist journal cannot be deleted. Not even a super admin is exempt — both apps connect as the same restricted database role.

isolation.title: One center cannot read another's rows
isolation.body: Enforced by row-level security policies in PostgreSQL, not by an if-statement in application code. A query that forgets its filter returns nothing rather than everything.

minors.title: Default-minor, everywhere it matters
minors.body: One positive condition decides adulthood, so a missing field, an unverified date or a new column can never silently unlock a child's account.

sessions.title: Deactivation ends a session in the same statement
sessions.body: A database trigger deletes a user's sessions whenever their status changes, they are soft-deleted, or their token version bumps — so it holds even for SQL that never goes through the application.

analytics.title: IDs only, and minors are never identified at all
analytics.body: No name, email, phone or anything a human typed reaches an analytics vendor. Session replay and autocapture are off, and single-use tokens are redacted before an error ever leaves the browser.
